title: Java Polymorphism
learningObjectives: Define polymorphism as one common type supporting multiple implementations.
Use a superclass reference to refer to a subclass object.
Explain method overriding and runtime method dispatch.
Distinguish an object's runtime type from a variable's declared type.
Use polymorphism to write code that works with different implementations.

understand.concept: Polymorphism allows a superclass reference or interface reference to refer to objects of different concrete classes. When an overridden instance method is called, Java selects the implementation based on the object's runtime class.
understand.whyItMatters: Polymorphism lets calling code depend on a stable abstraction rather than concrete class details. New implementations can often be added without rewriting the code that uses the common type.
understand.analogy: Think of a well-designed object as a small service with a clear responsibility: it keeps the information it owns and exposes only the operations other code needs.
understand.analogyLimit: This analogy is only a design aid; Java access, inheritance and dispatch follow the language's exact rules.

explain.narrative:
## Parent references and child objects

A variable declared with a parent type can refer to an instance of a child type. The declared type controls which members are available at compile time; the runtime object determines which overridden instance method runs.

## Method overriding

A subclass overrides an inherited instance method by providing a compatible signature. Use `@Override` so the compiler can check the intention.

## Runtime dispatch

Java selects an overridden instance method at runtime. Static methods are hidden rather than overridden, and fields are not dynamically dispatched.

## Common mistakes

- Confusing overloading with overriding.
- Assuming the declared reference type changes the actual object.
- Expecting fields or static methods to use runtime dispatch.

questions.prompt: Which method implementation runs for an overridden instance method?
questions.answer: The implementation belonging to the runtime object
options: The implementation belonging to the runtime object
The first method in the file
questions.explanation: Runtime dispatch selects the method based on the actual object.

questions.prompt: What does @Override help the compiler check?
questions.answer: That a method overrides an inherited method
options: That a method overrides an inherited method
questions.explanation: The annotation detects many accidental signature mismatches.

questions.prompt: What controls which members are available through a reference at compile time?
questions.explanation: Compile-time member access is checked against the declared type.

questions.prompt: Are static methods overridden with runtime dispatch?
questions.answer: No, static methods are hidden rather than overridden
options: No, static methods are hidden rather than overridden
